  A petition was received with over 1500 signatures and filed in the Office of the
  City Clerk entitled: We the Citizens of La Verne want to have a ballot measure
  presented on the next election as follows:

  We are requesting that the City Council suspend any decision regarding
  conversion of the La Verne Fire Department to the Los Angeles County Fire
  Department until after the above initiative has been voted on by the Citizens of
  La Verne.

  The People of the City of La Verne do ordain as follows: Paramedic/ Fire
  services and Police services shall be City employees directly reporting to the
  City as employees and the City shall not contract with a private company or
  county services without a vote by the citizens approving such action.

  The City Council discussed at length the matter of placing a measure on the
  2022 ballot for fire services for La Verne.  They also discussed placing a
  second measure stating that before any decision is made regarding
  contracting out public safety, it will need to be ratified by the La Verne
  residents.

  It was moved by Council Member Davis seconded by Crosby, and
  unanimously carried by roll call ( 5- 0) that before an agreement for services
  with Los Angeles County Fire was executed; it would be put on an election
  by the voters. In addition, the matter of the second
  ballot for ratification
  measure was tabled for discussion for a future Council meeting.

 Honorable  Mayor Tim Hepburn,  members  of  the la Verne  City Council,  and  staff:

I would  like to speak in favor of the motion to place a measure on the 2022 ballot that requests
La Verne  residents  be allowed  to vote  on  whether  they wish to contract for fire and paramedic
services with either Los Angeles County Fire or retain these services with city employees.

At age 93, and  on  the evening of what turned out to be the last  month  of  his life, my father fell

at our  home, breaking his hip and  hitting his head. City paramedics were at our house almost
beforewe had an  opportunitytocradle  hishead and movefurnituresotheycould stabilize him
for hospital transport. If you have ever  experienced  an  event  like this, time seems to slow to a

crawl  while  simultaneously  racing  by like lightening. A contingent  of paramedics  attended  to

getting my dad ready for hospital transport; he was  made  comfortable  while  my husband and I
answered  questions.  Besides  my  panic,  what I chiefly remember was the reassurance I felt from
these competent  and  compassionate  professionals  who  arrived  so  quickly  and  helped us on this

step of my dad' s last journey.
This decision to choose  our  fire and paramedic services is critical to quality of life for La Verne
residents and should not be imposed on us without thorough examination of the pros and cons
of  both options.  I am  proud  that La Verne is so responsive  to its residents  and  would  hope that

this value  continues  to be reflected  in a careful  analysis  of a  decision that simply  cannot  be

revoked  once  it is made.  If a decision is made to commit to fire and paramedic services through
Los Angeles  County, it would  be fiscally impossible to return to city- run services if v e are
dissatisfied with the outcome.  When La Verne  residents  voted  to increase  our  sales  tax, we  d id

so  for the express  purpose  of  supporting  our  local public safety  services,  including fire and
paramedic services.

Allow the citizens  of  La Verne to make the determination,  through  the ballot, to choose  from

whom  we  receive  fire and  paramedic  services;  La Verne  voters  deserve this courtesy. Thank you

for your time.

Public Comments  on Item 7b

Good evening Counci) Members, Mr Russi

In previous presentations I have presented the financial obligations that the City will face if
entering into the Contract Proposal with  Los Angeles County Fire District.  In analyzing the
financial obligations, I followed exactly the process outlined in the LACFD Feasibility
Study/ Contract Proposal, Page 11, under the Section Title Annual Fee Payment Cap.

Several weeks ago, I emailed to each Council Member an Excel spreadsheet with those details
and calculations for your review, along with additional comments.

Under the LACFD Contract Proposal the City would pay to the County 7. 5 million dollars more
than  it would  cost  to  maintain  LVFD at its projected  costs.  This does not include  the millions  of

dollars the City stands to lose from medical insurance revenue that has been coming to the City
for decades for the Rescue Ambulance transportation, which would instead go to private
ambulance  services.

The LACFD Contract  Proposal  costs for an additional  10 year contract would exceed the amount
projected to maintain LVFD by 85. 5 Million dollars, and and the loss of additional millions of
dollars from medical insurance for Ambulance transportation.

This does not even address the substantial reduction in what is by far the most used service
  Transportation.  Under LACFD,
from LVFD which  is Paramedic  Emergency Medica) Response  and

there would be at most 3 paramedics on duty in the City, and they outsource the ambulance
transportation. In contrast, under even minimal staffing LVFD has 9 paramedics on duty in the
City with Rescue Ambulance transportation, and with traditional staffing LVFD would have 11
paramedics  on  duty  at  all  times.  This is vitally important when in a short period of time you
have  several  medical  emergencies  and/  or  multiple  victims  of  violence.  Bringing in a paramedic
squad from Pomona, Claremont, or San Dimas is a huge delay in emergency medical response
because it would take several minutes for any of those squads to even get to the outer city
boundaries of La Verne and then being able to get the private ambulances on scene timely.

Additionally, the contract costs would be hidden and not be available for La Verne residents to
view and analyze as the money would be taken from Property Taxes by a tax assignment, prior
  the  balance of the  property  tax  proceeds.  That is documented  in
to the  City receiving
